## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `property-lifetime-evidence-retention`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-09T13:39:47.942Z.

Context relevance ledger (34): property-lifetime conditioned evidence retention — the relevance of a recorded fact decays with the lifetime of the property it describes, never with the lifetime of the item that recorded it, and an assembler that treats a closed owner as evidence of staleness makes the same category error that retired a live guard in pm-5z9plz.

Recorded 2026-08-09. Candidate only, routed through pm-g8t7b9 like every other entry in this ledger, and explicitly not weighted on the single incident that motivated it.

The signal. Every retrieval heuristic this project has considered treats an item's terminal status as a decay input, which is right for evidence about the work and wrong for evidence about the record. A closed item that measured a population, declared a bound, or established a corpus-wide invariant is describing something that outlives it: the population is still there, the bound is still meaningful, the invariant is still checkable. A closed item that describes its own progress, its own blockers, or its own review thread is describing something that ended when it ended. These are different retention classes and the corpus currently carries no marker separating them, so a single decay curve over closed_at necessarily over-retains the second and under-retains the first.

The proposal is a per-annotation retention class derived from what the annotation refers to rather than from who authored it. An annotation whose subject is a corpus-level property, detectable because it names a selector, a count over the whole record, a contract, or a gate, retains full weight after its owner terminates. An annotation whose subject is the item's own execution decays normally. The classifier is deliberately conservative: unclassifiable annotations take the existing decay, so the signal can only ever rescue evidence from premature decay and never accelerate it.

Why this is not entry (26) or (32). Entry (26) conditions retrieval on recurrence, which asks whether a defect came back; this asks whether a fact is still about anything. Entry (32) conditions confidence on the epoch a contract was emitted under, which asks whether a reader is competent to interpret a record; this asks whether the referent of the record still exists. A fact can be perfectly interpretable under the current epoch and describe a property that was deleted, and it can be uninterpretable and describe a property that is very much alive.

Degeneracy clauses, mandatory as for every entry in this ledger. The term is identically neutral on a corpus with no terminal items, because there is nothing whose decay could be adjusted. It is identically neutral when no annotation classifies, which is the state of the corpus today, so shipping the classifier changes no ranking until classification exists. It is retention-only and may never raise an annotation's weight above what it carried while its owner was active, so the signal cannot be used to make a closed item outrank a live one. And on a corpus where every closed item's annotations classify as corpus-level, it degenerates to disabling terminal decay entirely, which must be a detectable and reportable state rather than a silent one, because that is the shape a misclassifier would produce.

The measurable claim, so this can be falsified rather than admired. Two thousand and thirty-six closed items hold the large majority of the record's annotations. If the classifier is real, a held-out set of questions answerable only from closed-item annotations should show a retrieval improvement concentrated entirely in the corpus-level class and no movement at all in the execution class. If the improvement is spread evenly, the classifier is reading authorship or age rather than reference, and the entry should be withdrawn.

Scope clarification from individual-ownership review: pm-5z9plz owns a related measurement, read primitive or defect fix. It does not independently deliver this proposed ranking behavior. Reuse its evidence and public API; evaluate the additional behavior in this experiment.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.

Define a versioned public-SDK input/output and parameter contract, with exact source receipts and bounded time, memory and token complexity.; Implement an isolated reproducible prototype and compare held-out quality, task success, costs, cold-start behavior and negative controls against the unchanged baseline.; Record an accept, reject, or defer decision with evidence; production implementation requires an accepted decision and its own linked delivery scope.
A falsifiable decision on property lifetime evidence retention with reusable benchmark evidence and no unreviewed production policy change.
